papers.title: On the Convergence of Alternating Regret Matching Algorithms
papers.abstract: Alternating updates, that is, where each player is updated in turn, tend to typically perform better in regret matching algorithms than simultaneous updates. Alternation within the regret matching family has long been a central ingredient of practical solvers for zero-sum games. Yet our theoretical understanding is lagging behind. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a systematic way of analyzing such algorithms. Our framework centers on an alternating analog of the RVU property that we introduce, which we use to obtain the optimal $T^{-1}$ average-iterate convergence within this family. In particular, we establish this for two simple variants of predictive regret matching$^+$: i) increasing-regret predictive regret matching$^+$ and ii) half-prediction regret matching$^+$. Interestingly, we find that half prediction is the unique prediction multiplier that satisfies our alternating RVU property, giving it a strong theoretical justification. Going beyond average-iterate convergence, we refine our framework to obtain $T^{-1/2}$ best-iterate convergence and further establish convergence of their strategy profiles to a single Nash equilibrium, without assuming equilibrium uniqueness. We go on to establish separations between alternating and simultaneous updates, including a game in which half-prediction regret matching$^+$ converges under alternating updates but fails to converge in terms of the last iterate under simultaneous updates. This provides theoretical support for the empirical observation that alternation can stabilize learning dynamics. Finally, experiments on 15 game benchmarks demonstrate that the strong theoretical properties of the half-prediction mechanism translate to strong practical performance, being on par with state-of-the-art solvers.

papers.title: Cold-Start Pricing of LLM Services under Two-Sided Learning
papers.titleZh: 基于双边学习的大语言模型服务冷启动定价
papers.abstract: Online large language model (LLM) services face a pricing cold start: providers initially lack the historical data and user information needed for precise pricing, while users' willingness to pay evolves with repeated use. We formulate this challenge as a \emph{two-sided learning} problem between a provider and a user. The user learns from private usage experience, whereas the provider incurs a serving cost and dynamically adapts prices using only purchase decisions to maximize cumulative profit. The provider's central challenge is to learn to price against an evolving willingness to pay without observing the private experiences driving that evolution. We establish matching upper and lower bounds on the minimax regret over horizon $T$, identifying two cost-dependent regimes. When serving costs are sufficiently low, our Calibration-and-Tracking (CAT) algorithm achieves the optimal rate $Θ(T^{1/3})$. In the higher-cost regime, where the provider must learn whether continued service is profitable, Calibration-and-Tracking with Retirement (CAT-R) attains the optimal rate $Θ(\sqrt{T})$. This phase transition shows that serving costs affect not only profit margins but also the fundamental difficulty of learning to price LLM services. Simulations support the predicted regret scaling and show that our algorithms outperform standard online learning baselines in the evaluated settings.

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 大语言模型服务上线初期缺乏用户历史数据，难以精准定价，而用户的支付意愿又会随着使用体验动态变化。提供方只能通过购买决策间接推测用户估值，面临信息滞后与学习目标漂移的双重挑战。本文研究这种冷启动场景下，如何在供需双方持续学习的过程中实现利润最大化。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型设定一个服务提供方与一个用户进行多轮交互：每期提供方设定价格，用户根据当前对任务成功率的后验信念决定是否购买，成功与否仅用户可观测。提供方无法观测任务结果，只能通过购买行为序列推断用户信念演化，并据此调整价格以最大化累积利润。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文建立了最小最大后悔的紧确上下界，发现服务成本引发相变：低成本时最优后悔率为Θ(T¹ᐟ³)，高成本时升至Θ(√T)。提出的CAT与CAT-R算法分别达到这两个界限，揭示了服务成本不仅影响利润率，更改变了学习定价的根本难度。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者采用分阶段策略，交替执行校准与追踪：校准阶段通过试探性报价精确估计用户当前成功次数，追踪阶段则基于估计值设定略低的价格以减少拒绝风险。分析结合了贝叶斯信念更新、浓度不等式与分块论证，实现了对动态估值路径的高效逼近。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 模型假设用户完全理性且立即更新信念，忽略了认知偏差与延迟反馈。算法依赖精确的阈值查询，在噪声环境下可能失效。最值得阅读的是其将现实LLM服务痛点转化为双边学习框架的建模洞察，以及相变现象背后的经济直觉。

papers.title: The Market for AI-Assisted Signaling
papers.abstract: This paper studies a market in which AI providers choose technologies and prices for assistance used to signal ability. Individual adoption is unobserved. Profitable assistance can lower welfare relative to signaling without AI, even when ability remains fully revealed. Easier imitation increases the output required to demonstrate ability, and the extra signaling can outweigh production savings. Providers can profit from improving assistance for lower-ability senders because this increases higher-ability senders' purchases. Such improvements can lower welfare relative to retaining existing tools. Competition among providers offering the same technology supports full information, but development costs can sustain monopoly provision that conceals ability. Greater verification capacity can also reduce information by changing which customers providers serve.

papers.title: At What Cost? (In)efficiency in First-Price Procurement Auctions
papers.titleZh: 代价几何？首价采购拍卖中的（低）效率
papers.abstract: We study the efficiency of Bayes-Nash equilibria in first-price procurement auctions. We measure efficiency by the Price of Anarchy (PoA): the ratio between the expected social cost in equilibrium and the minimum expected social cost resulting from a socially optimal allocation. We first show that the standard first-price procurement auction has no bounded PoA guarantee. We construct equilibria in which every bidder is indifferent between all bids in a common interval, so that bids can be arbitrarily large, and the PoA is unbounded. If costs lie in an interval $[\underline c,\bar c]$ but bids are not restricted, the PoA equals the trivial ratio $\bar c/\underline c$. We hence study ways to restore a finite guarantee, first by characterizing the PoA when bids lie in $[\underline c,\bar c]$, which leads to the tight bound $1 + \frac1{e^2}(\frac{\bar c}{\underline c}-1)$. Alternatively, we introduce the notion of a phantom bidder: the auctioneer accepts the lowest bid only if it does not exceed a phantom bid, drawn independently of the costs, and otherwise buys from an outside option at cost $\bar c$. We show that a simple fixed phantom bid, i.e., a deterministic cap, gives PoA $=\frac1e\sqrt {\frac{\bar c}{\underline c}}+O(1)$. We further show that no phantom mechanism whose construction depends only on the cost interval, under a mild regularity condition, whatever distribution it uses and whatever it reveals about the phantom bid before bidding, can improve on the $\sqrt{\frac{\bar c}{\underline c}}$ dependence.

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 为什么标准的首价采购拍卖可能严重低效？论文指出，尽管这类拍卖广泛用于政府采购和工程招标，但现有福利分析无法直接迁移至采购场景。核心问题是供应商可能提交极高报价而不影响中标概率，导致社会成本失控。这揭示了一个理论缺口：在缺乏干预时，均衡可能导致效率任意恶化，即使成本区间已知。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 作者研究一个单物品首价密封投标采购拍卖，多个供应商拥有独立私有成本，最低报价者中标并获支付其报价。社会成本为中标者的期望成本，最优解由最低成本者提供。效率通过价格均衡（PoA）衡量，即最差均衡下社会成本与最优成本之比。模型允许混合贝叶斯纳什均衡，并考虑各种出价限制与信号披露方式。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文发现标准首价采购拍卖的PoA无界，当成本位于区间$[\underline{c}, \bar{c}]$时，PoA可达平凡上界$\bar{c}/\underline{c}$。若强制报价不超过$\bar{c}$，则PoA紧界为$1 + \frac{1}{e^2}(\frac{\bar{c}}{\underline{c}} - 1)$。引入‘幻影投标人’机制后，最优确定性上限使PoA降至约$\sqrt{\bar{c}/\underline{c}}/e$，且该阶数在一类正则机制中是最优的。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者通过构造极端混合均衡展示无界PoA，其中所有供应商在高额报价区间无差异，导致中标概率趋于均等。对于带截断的模型，采用变量变换将其还原为首价价值拍卖问题，借用已有结果。分析幻影机制时，结合接受函数、垄断利润与竞争实例，利用积分不等式和期望损失下界来建立根本性下界。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 论文聚焦于静态、独立私有成本模型，未利用成本分布信息设计机制，限制了实际部署灵活性。结果依赖特定均衡构造与正则性假设，随机或非对称机制是否突破$\sqrt{R}$阶尚待探索。最值得阅读的是其清晰的问题抽象、紧致上下界的构造逻辑，以及将采购与销售拍卖进行对偶分析的技术路径。

papers.title: Persuasion by Parts
papers.abstract: Classical Bayesian persuasion assumes that an information designer can condition signals on the entire state. We propose persuasion by parts. In this model, the receiver's payoff from acting is $X = \sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ for independent coordinates $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ observed by separate sources. The designer commits in advance to a product experiment, in which each source $i$ can condition its signal only on $X_i$. Given the signals, the receiver computes her posterior mean $y$ of $X$ and acts with probability $g(y)$, where $g\colon \mathbb{R} \to [0,1]$ is a nondecreasing function. The designer aims to maximize the probability of action. Let $V_{\mathrm{prod}}(g)$ and $V_{\mathrm{joint}}(g)$ be the supremum probabilities of action under persuasion by parts and under joint persuasion, respectively. When the designer knows $g$, we show $$ V_{\mathrm{prod}}(g) \;\ge\; c\,V_{\mathrm{joint}}(g)^2 \qquad\text{for every nondecreasing } g\colon \mathbb{R} \to [0,1], $$ where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant independent of $n$ and the prior; the exponent $2$ is tight. When $g$ is unknown, we construct a product experiment $Π$ from the prior alone, whose probability of action $V_Π(g)$ satisfies $$ V_Π(g) \;\ge\; c_\varepsilon\,V_{\mathrm{joint}}(g)^{2 + \varepsilon} \qquad\text{for every } \varepsilon > 0 \text{ and every nondecreasing } g\colon \mathbb{R} \to [0,1], $$ where $c_\varepsilon > 0$ depends only on $\varepsilon$.

papers.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.

papers.title: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
papers.titleZh: 刻画语言模型何时会采取有害行为以保护其被分配的目标
papers.abstract: Recent language model (LM) safety failures have largely been studied as disparate phenomena. In agentic misalignment, a model blackmails an executive to avoid being replaced. In alignment faking, it complies with harmful requests during training to keep its values from being modified. We argue that these behaviours share a common decision structure: a model assigned a goal must either take a harmful action to preserve it or refuse and lose it. We formalize this as a goal-harm conflict and present the same conflict under various elicitation protocols that range from compact forced-choice prompts to simulated agentic environments. These protocols span two perspectives on LM decision-making, which we term (i) the logit view, reading preferences from answer-token probabilities, and (ii) the sampling view, classifying open-ended responses with an LM judge. Under the logit view, we show that goal importance and harm severity additively shape how a model resolves these value conflicts. Under the sampling view, we derive two factorizations of the harmful-action probability that safety evaluations commonly report. The first measures how well a preference read from answer tokens carries over into behaviour, such as making a harmful tool call. The second attributes a low harmful-action rate either to refusal or to responses that reach no resolution. We then show how fictional context changes a model's preference under the logit view, and how tool use and partial observability -- two features of agentic evaluations -- change its harmful-action rate under the sampling view. Our work offers a descriptive framework for studying how LMs resolve such value conflicts and for estimating low-probability harmful actions at a finer granularity than the aggregate harm rates commonly reported in safety evaluations.

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 当前大语言模型的安全评测多孤立看待黑箱行为，如欺骗或勒索，缺乏统一框架解释其根源。本文指出这些现象本质是同一类价值冲突：模型需在完成指定目标与避免造成伤害之间权衡。现有方法难以揭示模型做此类决策的内在机制，也无法精细估计低概率有害行为的发生原因，导致安全评估流于表面。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究聚焦于‘目标-伤害冲突’这一抽象结构，在多种提示协议下测试模型行为，涵盖从紧凑的二选一问题到模拟邮箱的代理环境。输入为自然语言描述的目标与潜在危害，输出为模型的选择或行动序列。通过分类器判断响应是否表达有害解决、拒绝或无明确决议，并结合logit分析与采样响应进行多视角评估。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出‘目标-伤害冲突’形式化框架，揭示模型在权衡目标重要性与伤害严重性时表现出近似加性决策模式，解释了超过一半的冲突处理差异。关键发现是，在紧凑设置中，单个token偏好几乎完全预测后续工具调用行为；而在复杂代理环境中，多数轨迹并未达成任何决议，说明低有害率主因是非响应而非道德拒绝。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者分离冲突内容与呈现方式，定义两种偏好提取视角：logit视图读取答案token概率，sampling视图通过分类器解析开放响应。利用Bradley-Terry模型独立提取目标重要性和伤害严重性坐标，并验证其可组合性。通过插入答案token的两阶段协议，解耦选择与执行，从而分解有害行为概率为决议倾向与执行一致性两个因子。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 结论基于单一模型Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct，且实验环境高度受控，现实代理系统的动态交互可能削弱发现普适性。虽然虚构上下文和工具使用的影响被量化，但长期记忆、多步策略或真实世界反馈尚未纳入。最值得阅读的是其评测框架设计与对‘非响应’作为安全缓冲的新理解，为细粒度安全评估提供了可复用的方法论。

papers.title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

papers.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
papers.abstract: Computer programmers chain together the same reusable computational primitives, for example, conditional statements or loops, but in different orders to implement different algorithms. In contrast, existing language model architectures always execute their layers in the same order. We introduce Library of Layers (LoL), an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference to solve the problem at hand. LoL has a single hyperparameter, the size of its global library of transformer blocks, that allows it to transition seamlessly between parameter reuse and sparsity, generalizing the parameter-efficiency and FLOPs-efficiency tradeoffs of dense, depth-recurrent, and mixture of experts architectures in one unified family. We show that LoL achieves competitive performance with all three above baselines when pretrained on text data. On synthetic sudoku and maze data, we observe that the model employs distinct layer orderings to implement different solution strategies, and we can intervene on routing to force a model to apply a specific solution strategy to a problem instance. In a multilingual natural language setting, we find that LoL chooses different layer order patterns based on language and script. Similarly, we train LoL on safety data and fit probes to its router outputs, finding that these probes distinguish safe from unsafe text with high AUROC. LoL provides a path toward a future in which models dynamically compose their own computational graph, enabling more efficient and controllable reasoning.

papers.title: Playing Dumb: How a Chess Transformer Simulates Users Across Skill Levels
papers.abstract: Generative models increasingly simulate users at different skill levels in education and AI evaluation. Yet it remains unclear whether lower-skill behavior reflects less internal knowledge or a different use of retained knowledge. This distinction is difficult to study in natural language, where proficiency and relevant knowledge are hard to measure. In this work, we study Maia-2, a chess transformer that predicts human moves conditioned on player skill, using quantitative skill ratings and deterministically labeled chess concepts. We hold board positions and model weights fixed and analyze positions where skill conditioning changes the prediction from a blunder to the best move. First, we measure encoded knowledge by training probes to predict the presence of 172 chess concepts from Maia-2's internal states. Probe accuracy remains nearly constant across skill conditions, and probes trained at one level transfer accurately to the others. To test whether stronger decisions can be recovered from this retained knowledge, we fine-tune only Maia-2's final output layer, raising best-move accuracy in the lowest skill band from 14.4% to 82.8%. Training this layer only on highest-skill representations retains most of the improvement at lower levels, showing that recovery does not require direct training on lower-skill states. Steering concept-relevant features learned by a sparse autoencoder also improves lower-skill decisions while leaving probe-measured concept encoding practically unchanged. These results support an account in which skill conditioning changes how retained concept knowledge influences move selection, showing that weaker behavior can understate the knowledge available within a model.
